anti_overlap: Leave citation fidelity to fd-stemmatics-witness-collation: do not audit whether f-NNN ids exist in the melange synthesis, whether the '30 upheld prescriptions' count matches, which upheld findings have no disposition, or whether the Amendments say what the plan reports them as saying

Leave the entity register's substance to fd-stemmatics-witness-collation: duplicate/phantom/historical country codes, the TAN/TZA/ZNZ collision, source and `accessed`-date discipline, the 2025-12-31 currency vs 2025-01-01 t=0 dating question, and roster naming

Do not review the simulation's modelling choices (which institutions are realistic, whether the issue roster is well-chosen, whether the situations are interesting); confine judgment to whether measurements and certificates mean what they claim
Do not restate general 'add more tests' advice; every finding must name the specific check, standard, or tolerance that fails to discriminate, and say what would have come out differently
decision_lens: For each check in this plan, ask: could this have failed? Who held the standard it was measured against, and was that party independent of the work? Was the instrument calibrated before the measurement or repaired afterward? Was the tolerance written down in advance, with a rule for recording deviations, or is it decided at the bench by the person being measured? If the answer is that the process certifies itself, the finding is severe regardless of how many steps the protocol has.
distance_rationale: Assay practice is a legal-administrative craft of physical standards, not a science of systems, information, or organisms — and none of its load-bearing doctrines are reachable from software-testing intuition. Its whole subject is the question of who is permitted to certify whom: the assayer must not be the mint; the trial plate must be sealed by an authority independent of the party being tried; a balance adjusted between two weighings invalidates both; a stamp records that an assay happened, it never substitutes for one; and a tolerance is worthless unless written down before the piece is weighed. This plan re-mints its own reference standard (`strabo-r0-baseline`) immediately after repairing the very instrument (`referee.sh`) that will use it, has each Wave A task certify itself with the un-repaired instrument, and permits an intentional failure of its new data leg on a prose disclosure. That is the exact family of defect the Pyx procedure was invented to make impossible, and the assay tradition has three centuries of vocabulary for it that no software-quality frame supplies.
expected_isomorphisms: Trial plate held by an independent authority <-> `strabo-r0-baseline` as the reference the referee is compared against; here the plate is struck by the same hands, at the same moment, as the repaired instrument that will read it

The assayer must not be the mint <-> Task 2 and Task 3 modify `scripts/bench/divergence/referee.sh` inside the same waves whose output that script is meant to adjudicate; no arm's-length check certifies the referee itself

Calibrate the balance BEFORE the weighing, never after <-> Task 1's pre/post baseline-shift diff (Step 6) is taken before Task 3 removes the HashMap iteration nondeterminism and before Task 2 adds the data stamp, so the diff is read on an instrument known to be both blind and jittery

Written remedy (allowable deviation, fixed in advance, recorded per assay) <-> the ±10% decisions-per-leg-year band, the 'at_ceiling < len/10' threshold, the >0.5 variance floor — which of these are stated in advance with a recording rule, and which are improvised at the bench
Sealed, tamper-evident custody of the standard <-> a lightweight, movable, unsigned `git tag`; the SHA is recorded in a prose README that can diverge from the tag it names

The verification stamp records provenance, it does not perform the weighing <-> `data_manifest` is a hash label; the plan credits it with detection power that the arm-vs-arm build comparison already supplies, and tests the label rather than the assay

Sample selection determines what the assay can find (which coins go in the pyx box) <-> which seeds, which strategies, which scripted leg constitute the certification set; seeds 1000/2000 vs 1000/2000/3000 drift between the protocol section, Task 3, and Task 17

A gauge that rejects conforming work and passes non-conforming work is worse than no gauge <-> `<verify>` blocks built on `grep -c ... expect contains "1"`, which a thorough implementation overshoots and a one-line comment satisfies
focus: Whether the plan's measuring apparatus — the referee protocol, the re-minted baseline, the per-task <verify> blocks, the acceptance-criteria ```check``` commands, and the tolerances they enforce — constitutes a valid assay of the claim 'refereed real-world grounding', or whether the instrument, the standard, and the certificate are all produced by the process under test.
name: fd-assay-baseline-integrity
persona: Apply the perspective of an assay master and weights-and-measures inspector: someone whose trade is deciding whether a certificate means anything. This perspective reads a verification protocol the way a Pyx jury reads a mint's paperwork — asking who struck the standard, who held it, whether the balance was adjusted between weighings, whether the tolerance was written before or after the piece was weighed, whether the sample submitted for trial was drawn by the party being tried, and whether the stamp on the finished work certifies the property it appears to certify or merely records that someone was present. It treats a gauge that a correct implementation fails, or that a token comment passes, as a defect in the gauge, not in the workpiece. It is unimpressed by the quantity of verification steps and interested only in whether any single one could have come out the other way.
review_areas: Standard and custody: how `strabo-r0-baseline` is minted, held, and referenced — Task 5 tags after the same wave that rewrites the referee, the tag is lightweight and movable, the SHA lives in prose, and nothing outside the plan can re-derive it; ask what an independent party could check the rung against

Calibration order across Wave A: Task 1's Step 6 baseline-shift diff, Task 2's manifest, and Task 3's determinism fix are mutually dependent instruments certified in an order the Execution Handoff then declares 'independent (parallelizable)' — establish which measurements are taken on an instrument the plan itself says is broken

Gauge validity of every `<verify>` block and every ```check``` fence: whether the command can distinguish conforming from non-conforming work at all, whether `grep -c` line counts penalize thorough implementations, whether a zero-count grep's non-zero exit is read as failure, and whether AC 10/11/12/14 have any executable check

Whether the R1-data leg detects anything the existing arm-vs-arm comparison does not: referee.sh builds the OLD arm from a detached worktree at the given commit, so `data/` edits are already compiled into the binary — trace what the manifest actually adds, and whether Task 7's stated 'code leg passes while the data leg reports a delta' can physically occur

Tolerances and overrides: the ±10% decisions/leg-year band, the ceiling and variance thresholds in Task 1's test, and — critically — the unbounded 'intentional' data-manifest delta in Task 7, which permits the new gate to fail on prose disclosure with no allowlist, expected-manifest file, or recording rule specified

Sample sufficiency and cost of the trial: which seeds, ticks, strategies and arms constitute certification; the seed set drifts between the protocol section, Task 3 and Task 17; a two-seed × two-replay battery at TICKS=8766 with two release builds has a runtime the plan never budgets, and an unbudgeted assay is one that gets skipped

severity_examples.condition: P0 whenever the plan's central evidence mechanism cannot produce the evidence it is specified to produce, or two ratified sections demand opposite outcomes from the same gate
severity_examples.scenario: Task 7 states the register consolidation will show 'R1 code-leg passes, R1-data leg reports the manifest delta intentionally — that asymmetry is the entire point of Task 2'. But referee.sh builds the OLD arm from a detached worktree at the supplied commit, and Task 2 Step 1 makes the loaders embed-only, so a `data/` change is compiled into the binary and moves the simulation; the code leg cannot pass. The rung's showcase demonstration of its own new instrument is architecturally impossible, and Acceptance Criterion 9 ('manifests match') directly contradicts the task that is supposed to exercise the leg.

severity_examples.condition: P1 when a verify block's pass/fail is anti-correlated with, or independent of, the property the task exists to establish
severity_examples.scenario: Task 2's `<verify>` block runs `grep -c "data_manifest" scripts/bench/divergence/referee.sh` and expects the output to contain "1", while Step 4 of the same task requires extracting the manifest from BOTH arms and diffing them — an implementation that does what Step 4 says matches on two or more lines and fails its own verify block, whereas a single mention in a comment passes. The companion check `grep -c "read_to_string" gdp_baseline.rs` expecting "0" exits non-zero precisely when the task succeeded. The gauge rejects conforming work and passes non-conforming work.

severity_examples.condition: P2 when the reference standard is mutable or its recorded identity can drift from the artifact, degrading evidence quality without blocking the wave
severity_examples.scenario: `strabo-r0-baseline` is created with a bare `git tag` (lightweight, movable, unsigned) and its SHA is transcribed into `docs/research/strabo-r0/README.md` by hand, with no check that the two agree; every subsequent rung's byte-identity claim is anchored to a reference any later command can silently move.

source_domain: Assay-office and legal-metrology practice — the Trial of the Pyx (since 1282: coins set aside at strike time into a sealed box, assayed annually by a jury of goldsmiths against a trial plate held by a third party, never by the mint), the Exchequer standard yard and its witness copies, the verification stamp and the inspector's seal, the written 'remedy' (the tolerance a piece may deviate and still pass), and the traceability chain by which a shop's working gauge is tied back through a hierarchy of reference standards to a primary standard that no working process is allowed to touch.
success_hints: Read `scripts/bench/divergence/referee.sh` in full before judging Tasks 2, 3 and 7 — note `OLD=${1:?pre-change commit}`, the detached-worktree build of the OLD arm, `SEED=1000`, `TICKS=8766`, the `norm` invocations and the final `grep -q '^REFEREE PASS$'` gate; the plan's claims about what R1 currently can and cannot see must be checked against that file, not against the plan's own prose

Run each `<verify>` command and each ```check``` fence mentally against both a correct and a token implementation, and record which ones give the same verdict for both; `grep -c` counts LINES, and `grep -c` on zero matches exits 1

Confirm the current `grep -c "2000" scripts/bench/divergence/referee.sh` is 0 and consider what a bare literal '2000' would have to mean; then check whether the script's single-`SEED`/single-tracefile-naming structure can carry a second seed without restructuring the parts Task 3 does not list
Check the Execution Handoff's 'Wave A tasks 1-4 are independent (parallelizable)' against the referee-protocol section's ordering claims and Task 1 Step 6, Task 3 Step 3

Cross-index the Acceptance Criteria against the tasks: which criteria have no ```check``` fence, which fences assume a CLI contract no task specifies, and which fence's grep pattern (e.g. `grep -q "R1.*PASS"`) would match a line reporting partial failure

Look for the tolerance's recording rule, not just the tolerance: where does a permitted deviation (the ±10% band, Task 7's intentional manifest delta) get written down in a form a later reader can audit
task_context: Reviewing `docs/plans/2026-09-02-strabo-rung0-real-world-grounding.md` — a 17-task, 5-wave implementation plan for ShadowBench 'rung 0': four instrument repairs (referee data-plane blindness, budget_multiplier units saturation, HashMap determinism, ts-rs export fork), a `strabo-r0-baseline` re-baselining protocol, a canonical-2025 entity register audit, a model-what-exists institution roster with InstitutionType extension, flag-gated issue-to-situation injection, a 2025 snapshot, and a rung gate plus findings note. Goal: Find what makes this rung-0 plan fail and what it's missing: as an execution-grade plan for a weaker executor, do its tasks, verify blocks, and referee protocol actually deliver refereed real-world grounding, and where does it silently contradict the brainstorm Amendments, the melange prescriptions it claims to encode, or the codebase as it exists?
